ed860a050c.q: What is the difference between generative AI and agentic AI in healthcare?
ed860a050c.a: Generative AI creates artifacts like text or images. Agentic AI takes the next step: it reasons, reaches out into the world to get information or perform actions using tools, and operates with increasing amounts of autonomy. Large language models can reason in language, and when you give them tools, they become agents that can do tasks and work alongside healthcare providers.

f817f8b448.q: What are practical applications of agentic AI in medical practice operations?
f817f8b448.a: When a patient calls in or a referral comes through, an agent can help determine the right specialist, provide availability information, schedule the patient, and follow up if they miss an appointment. Agents can also optimize patient load distribution across providers in a clinic and handle higher-level operational thinking and optimization.

46825406ec.q: Why is explainability critical for physician adoption of agentic AI systems?
46825406ec.a: Explainability is critically important for doctors, patients, and everyone concerned because AI has to earn its trust and credibility in healthcare. Technologies like AI scribes work transparently because doctors see their words appearing, and tools like evidence synthesis show research that clinicians can assess themselves. As technologies improve clinicians' lives through demonstrated benefit, skepticism decreases.

abbe400386.q: What does technical humility mean in the context of AI developers entering healthcare?
abbe400386.a: Technical humility means not assuming you understand someone else's domain before understanding why things work the way they do in that field. Technologists must spend time with nurses, doctors, and care managers, develop empathy, and be prepared to change and evolve solutions based on what they learn, rather than racing to conclusions about outdated practices like beepers or faxes.
